claim_text: Microsoft says unauthorized parties accessed tenant-level metadata for affected organizations through a flaw in the Entra Connect Health API
summary: Microsoft's customer notification says its investigation, concluded Nov 20, found unauthorized read-only access to tenant-level metadata for the notified organizations.
detail: BleepingComputer and Borns IT- und Windows-Blog both quote or paraphrase the notification. A Microsoft statement to BleepingComputer says the issue 'could have resulted in unauthorized access to tenant-level contact and configuration metadata' and that affected customers were notified through Azure Service Health. This is Microsoft's own account, relayed from its customer notification; no outside party has checked it. We could not find the notification on a Microsoft site; the outlets say it was shared by administrators.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Two independent outlets report Microsoft's own notification, and Microsoft gave BleepingComputer a statement; the label records Microsoft's account, not an independent forensic check.
notes: Not Tier 1 because the notification text itself was not found on a Microsoft page.

claim_text: Microsoft says the flaw in the Entra Connect Health API was introduced on July 23, 2026 and discovered on Nov 9, 2026
summary: The notification dates the flaw's introduction to Jul 23 and its discovery to Nov 9.
detail: The outlets describe it as a vulnerability in the service API that could let an unauthorized party read tenant and service-monitoring metadata and possibly change Connect Health monitoring configuration. Microsoft has not said when exploitation began.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Reported by two independent outlets from Microsoft's own notification; dates are Microsoft's account.

claim_text: Microsoft says it deployed a server-side fix on Nov 19, 2026 and that customers need not install updates
summary: Microsoft says a server-side fix on Nov 19 closed the flaw and blocked further unauthorized access; no software update or other customer remediation is required to fix the vulnerability itself.
detail: Microsoft's statement to BleepingComputer also gives Nov 19 as the fix date.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Microsoft statement to an outlet plus two outlets quoting the notification; Microsoft's account only.

claim_text: Microsoft says it finished its investigation on Nov 20, 2026 and began notifying affected organizations through Azure Service Health
summary: Microsoft says it reviewed available telemetry for unauthorized API calls, concluded on Nov 20 and notified affected organizations.
detail: Microsoft's statement to BleepingComputer says affected customers were notified through Azure Service Health with guidance and support. Only tenants that received the notice are described as affected.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Two independent outlets and a Microsoft statement to one of them; Microsoft's account only.

claim_text: Microsoft says the exposed information was administrator and technical-contact email addresses and tenant configuration metadata
summary: Per the notification: technical-contact and administrator emails; tenant ID, name, domain, country, region; license tier; directory sync status; onboarding status.
detail: Microsoft also published read-only scripts for administrators to view these field types (see c009). This is Microsoft's own account, relayed from its customer notification; no outside party has checked it.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Two independent outlets list the same fields from Microsoft's notification; Microsoft's account only.

claim_text: Microsoft says an expired certificate once used to register Connect Health agents was also returned by the API
summary: The notification says the expired certificate was used with an internal Microsoft service decommissioned in late 2024; it was no longer in use but was still in Connect Health storage and returned by the API.
detail: Microsoft says the certificate was not in use. This is Microsoft's own account, relayed from its customer notification; no outside party has checked it.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Two independent outlets report this detail from Microsoft's notification; Microsoft's account only.

claim_text: Microsoft says no user passwords, password hashes, authentication tokens, valid cryptographic keys, on-premises server or Active Directory topology details, or Azure subscription information were exposed
summary: This is Microsoft's own statement of what was not exposed. It also says no Entra tenant data beyond the listed metadata was exposed.
detail: The statement is Microsoft's and has not been independently verified. Microsoft has not said how long the telemetry covers or how it knows what the callers did not see.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The label records that Microsoft says this (two independent outlets quote the notification), not an independent finding that nothing else was taken.
notes: Label reflects the statement, not proof of absence.

claim_text: Microsoft says it found no unauthorized configuration changes
summary: The notification says the investigation identified no unauthorized configuration changes, only read-only access.
detail: Outlets note the flaw could in principle have allowed changes to Connect Health monitoring configuration. Microsoft's account only.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Two independent outlets quote this from Microsoft's notification; Microsoft's account only.

claim_text: Microsoft recommends alerting security teams to phishing, using phishing-resistant MFA for privileged accounts, and reviewing audit and sign-in logs, and published read-only scripts
summary: Recommended steps: tell global admins, SOC and tenant technical contacts to watch for phishing and social engineering; require phishing-resistant MFA on privileged accounts; review Connect Health settings and Entra audit and sign-in logs.
detail: Microsoft's own GitHub page (s003) describes read-only PowerShell reference scripts to inspect the information the APIs return for a tenant. BleepingComputer says the script shows current values, not what was accessed in the breach.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Microsoft's own page (Tier 1) shows the scripts; two outlets report the recommended steps from the notification.
notes: The Tier 1 source supports the scripts; the steps rest on the outlets quoting the notification.

claim_text: More than a dozen administrators, including some managed service providers with several customer tenants, reported receiving the notice
summary: BleepingComputer says more than a dozen administrators said in a Reddit thread that they received the notification, and some managed service providers reported notices for multiple customer tenants.
detail: This is one outlet's description of a social media thread we did not read. It is not a count of affected organizations.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One Tier 2 outlet describes administrator posts; no official count exists.
notes: Not a tally of affected tenants.

claim_text: How many organizations or tenants were affected
summary: Microsoft has not said how many organizations were affected.
detail: BleepingComputer says Microsoft has not disclosed the number. Only organizations that received the notice are described as affected.
label: Not established

summary: Microsoft has not named or described who exploited the flaw.
detail: No outlet reports an attribution or any claim of responsibility.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: BleepingComputer says Microsoft has not disclosed who exploited the vulnerability.

claim_text: When the exploitation began and how long it lasted
summary: Microsoft has not said when attacks began. The flaw existed from Jul 23 to the Nov 19 fix, but exploitation in that window is not dated.
detail: The flaw's lifetime is not the same as the period of unauthorized access. A root cause beyond 'a vulnerability in the API' has not been published; one is needed before this story can close.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Microsoft has not given a start date for the unauthorized access.

claim_text: Whether the exposed administrator emails have been used in phishing or other follow-on attacks
summary: Microsoft warns of possible targeted phishing; no source reports a follow-on attack.
detail: We found no report of attacks that used the exposed data.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Microsoft says phishing is possible; no outlet reports any actual use.

claim_text: Whether this breach is linked to other Microsoft incidents, including the separate Microsoft 365 outage
summary: No source ties this breach to any other Microsoft incident.
detail: We found no official or independent source linking it to the Microsoft 365 outage or any other event, so the pages are not cross-linked.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the sources mention any link.
